definition_zh: 蒸散；蒸发蒸腾；地表水分经土壤蒸发与植物蒸腾共同进入大气的过程
definition_en: the combined transfer of water from the land surface to the atmosphere through evaporation from soil and open water and through transpiration from plants
core_image: 烈日下的农田向上吐出水汽：土面在蒸发，叶孔在蒸腾，两股看不见的水汽合为一股上升流
scene: 干旱区的试验田里，测量仪昼夜记录土面蒸发与作物叶片失水合成的总量。The lysimeter recorded evapotranspiration from the irrigated field around the clock.
sceneCN: 这里 evapotranspiration 指「地表水分经土壤蒸发与植物蒸腾共同进入大气的总量」（第 1 个义项：蒸发与蒸腾两条通道合成的水分输出）；句意为蒸渗仪昼夜不停记录这块灌溉田的蒸散量。图中可辨识物件：试验田、蒸渗仪、土面、作物叶片。

pos.zh: 蒸散；蒸发蒸腾（不可数，水文学与农学计量名词）

forms.label: 计量复数（不同地块的蒸散量）

derivatives.zh: 蒸散（技术文献中的罕见动词）

senses.title: The combined water loss from land to air
senses.titleCN: 地表向大气的水分总输出
senses.definition: the total flux of water from soil, open water and plant leaves into the atmosphere, counted as one process
senses.definitionCN: 土壤、自由水面与植物叶片进入大气的水分总通量，作为一个过程来计算
senses.example: The lysimeter recorded evapotranspiration from the irrigated field around the clock.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸渗仪昼夜不停记录这块灌溉田的蒸散量。
senses.why: The word is a deliberate blend of evaporation and transpiration, because hydrologists needed one label for two channels that leave the ground together and cannot be separated in the field.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是有意把 evaporation 与 transpiration 合在一起，因为水文学家需要一个名称来指两条同时离开地面、在野外无法分开的通道。

senses.title: The plant-only share of the flux
senses.titleCN: 其中由植物蒸腾贡献的部分
senses.definition: the portion of the flux that passes through stomata of living plants rather than through bare soil
senses.definitionCN: 经由活体植物气孔而非裸露土面进入大气的那一部分通量
senses.example: A wheat canopy gave transpiration the larger share of evapotranspiration.
senses.exampleCN: 在麦田冠层中，蒸腾占了蒸散的较大份额。
senses.why: Once the compound was in use, its two halves could be pulled apart again, and this sense names the plant half alone.
senses.whyCN: 复合词一旦通用，它的两半又可以被重新分开，这个义项就单指植物那一半。

senses.title: A measured depth of water per unit time
senses.titleCN: 以水深与时间表示的观测量
senses.definition: the quantity expressed as millimetres of water lost per day or per season over a defined area
senses.definitionCN: 在给定面积上以每天或每季损失的水深毫米数表示的量
senses.example: The station reported an evapotranspiration of six millimetres a day.
senses.exampleCN: 该观测站报告的蒸散量为每天六毫米。
senses.why: Hydrology turns processes into numbers, so the same noun came to name the measured depth rather than only the physical event.
senses.whyCN: 水文学把过程变成数字，因此同一个名词也从物理事件转而指测量所得的水深。

senses.title: Crop water demand in irrigation planning
senses.titleCN: 灌溉计划中的作物需水量
senses.definition: the water a crop must receive to replace what it loses through evapotranspiration
senses.definitionCN: 为补足作物蒸散损失而必须供给的水量
senses.example: Irrigation was timed to match the crop evapotranspiration each week.
senses.exampleCN: 灌溉按每周的作物蒸散量安排时间。
senses.why: In farm management the process becomes a demand to be met, since every millimetre lost must be replaced by rain or by the ditch.
senses.whyCN: 在农场管理中，这个过程变成必须满足的需求，因为每损失一毫米都得靠降雨或水渠补上。

senses.title: A term in the water-balance equation
senses.titleCN: 水量平衡方程中的输出项
senses.definition: the outflow term in a catchment water balance, set beside precipitation, runoff and storage change
senses.definitionCN: 流域水量平衡中的支出项，与降水、径流与蓄水量变化并列
senses.example: In the basin budget, evapotranspiration accounted for most of the rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 在流域水量收支中，蒸散占去了大部分降水。
senses.why: A budget must name every entry and exit; this sense fixes the word as the main exit in the accounting of a catchment.
senses.whyCN: 收支表必须给每一笔进出命名；这个义项把这个词固定为流域核算中的主要支出项。

senses.title: The latent-heat channel of the surface
senses.titleCN: 地表向大气的潜热通道
senses.definition: the same water flux viewed as latent heat that cools the surface and feeds the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 同一股水汽通量被看作潜热：它冷却地表并补给大气
senses.example: Satellites estimate evapotranspiration from the latent heat seen in thermal imagery.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星依据热红外影像中的潜热估算蒸散。
senses.why: Climate science reads the flux in energy units, because water leaving the surface carries heat away with it.
senses.whyCN: 气候学用能量单位读这股通量，因为离地的水把热量一并带走。

senses.title: Ecosystem water loss in ecology
senses.titleCN: 生态学中的生态系统失水
senses.definition: the water an ecosystem returns to the air, which determines streamflow, soil moisture and carbon uptake
senses.definitionCN: 生态系统返回大气的水量，它决定径流、土壤湿度与碳吸收
senses.example: Deforestation lowered evapotranspiration and raised the dry-season flow.
senses.exampleCN: 砍伐森林降低了蒸散，抬高了旱季流量。
senses.why: Ecology stresses the consequence rather than the mechanism: what leaves the ecosystem is water no longer available to streams and roots.
senses.whyCN: 生态学强调的是后果而非机制：离开生态系统的水，就不再可供溪流与根系使用。

senses.title: Any slow invisible drain from a system
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：系统里缓慢而不易察觉的流失
senses.definition: a gradual, unnoticed loss of a resource from a system, treated as if it were water rising away
senses.definitionCN: 资源从系统中缓慢、不易察觉地流失，被比作水汽升离地面
senses.example: The report described evapotranspiration of talent from the region.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把人才从该地区的外流描述为一种蒸散。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the physical shape: something valuable leaves quietly through many small openings, and the loss is noticed only in the ledger.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了物理形态：有价值之物经由许多小口悄然离去，直到看账本才发现少了。

intro.en: Evapotranspiration is a modern technical compound built from two older Latin-derived nouns, evaporation and transpiration. Each half has its own history; the compound itself is little more than a century old. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: evapotranspiration 是近代技术复合词，由两个更古老的拉丁来源名词 evaporation 与 transpiration 合成。两半各有自己的历史，复合词本身仅有百余年。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vapor meant 'steam, exhalation, vapour'. Its deeper origin is not established; the suggestion that it imitates the sound of steam is a hypothesis, so any older Indo-European form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: vapor 意为「蒸汽、呼出的气、雾汽」。其更深来源未得到证明；认为它模仿蒸汽之声的说法只是假说，因此凡为其给出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

items.en: The prefix e- 'out' plus vaporare 'to emit vapour' gave evaporare 'to vapourize'; Medieval Latin evaporatio and English evaporation followed in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 前缀 e-「向外」加 vaporare「放出汽」构成 evaporare「使汽化」；中世纪拉丁 evaporatio 与英语 evaporation 随后在十七世纪出现。

items.en: Spirare meant 'to breathe'. Its own origin is not settled; it is often placed beside a reconstructed root for blowing, but that form is a reconstruction rather than an attested word.
items.cn: spirare 意为「呼吸」。它本身的来源没有定论；常被放在一个表示「吹」的重构词根旁，但那个形式是重构而非有书证的词。

items.en: Trans- 'through' plus spirare produced transpirare 'to breathe through, to let vapour pass out'; English transpiration first named the escape of vapour through plant surfaces.
items.cn: trans-「穿过」加 spirare 构成 transpirare「透过…呼吸、让汽透出」；英语 transpiration 最初指水汽经植物表面逸出。

items.en: Agricultural meteorology and hydrology joined the two nouns into one term for the combined flux, because field instruments cannot separate the soil and leaf channels.
items.cn: 农业气象学与水文学把两个名词合成一个术语，用来指合并后的通量，因为野外仪器无法把土面与叶片两条通道分开。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only, and deeper origin of vapor and spirare): the compound entered print in the early twentieth century, but no single first citation is fixed, so the date is approximate; the roots behind vapor and spirare remain unsettled, and any forms offered for them are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代，以及 vapor 与 spirare 的更深词源）：该复合词在二十世纪初进入印刷品，但没有公认的最早书证，年代只能约计；vapor 与 spirare 背后的词根仍无定论，凡为其提出的形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same vapour or breathing stock that are easily confused with the two halves of this term; group two holds other water-balance processes that are often mistaken for it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「汽」或「呼吸」词干、容易与这个词的两半混淆的词；第二组是常被当作蒸散的其他水量平衡过程。

entries.definition: Loss of water as vapour from soil or open water without passing through a plant, so it names only one of the two channels.
entries.definitionCN: 水不经植物、直接从土面或自由水面化为水汽的损失，只指两条通道中的一条。

entries.definition: Water vapour leaving a plant through its stomata; standing alone it excludes direct evaporation from the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 水汽经植物气孔离开植物；单独使用时不含地面直接蒸发。

entries.definition: The physical change from liquid to vapour, a phase change rather than a land-surface flux.
entries.definitionCN: 由液态变为气态的物理变化，是相变而非地表通量。

entries.definition: Sweat, from Latin spirare through perspirare 'to breathe through'; it belongs to the same root but not to the water balance.
entries.definitionCN: 汗水，经拉丁 perspirare「透过呼吸」出自 spirare；与蒸散同根，但不属于水量平衡。

entries.definition: The water taken by a crop and not returned to the same basin; a planning term close to crop evapotranspiration.
entries.definitionCN: 作物取走且未回到同一流域的水量；是与作物蒸散接近的规划术语。

entries.definition: Direct change from snow or ice to vapour without melting; it bypasses the liquid stage that evaporation requires.
entries.definitionCN: 雪或冰不融化而直接变为水汽；它绕过了蒸发所需的液态阶段。

entries.definition: Change from vapour to liquid, the opposite direction of the same exchange between land and air.
entries.definitionCN: 由水汽变为液态，是陆地与大气之间同一交换的反方向。

entries.definition: Water that travels over the ground into streams; it is the other main exit from a catchment besides evapotranspiration.
entries.definitionCN: 沿地面流入溪流的水；是流域中除蒸散之外的另一主要支出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is evaporation plus transpiration, joined because instruments cannot split the two in the field.
normal.cn: 这个词就是 evaporation 加 transpiration，二者合称是因为野外仪器无法把它们分开。

normal.en: Vapor is 'steam'; spirare is 'to breathe'; trans- is 'through'.
normal.cn: vapor 是「蒸汽」；spirare 是「呼吸」；trans- 是「穿过」。

normal.en: The family runs evaporation, transpiration, vapor, vaporize and perspiration.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 evaporation、transpiration、vapor、vaporize 与 perspiration。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark measurement: actual, potential and reference evapotranspiration.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出计量方式：实际蒸散量、潜在蒸散量、参考作物蒸散量。

normal.en: Hydrology writes it as ET, a term in the water balance beside precipitation and runoff.
normal.cn: 水文学把它写作 ET，是水量平衡中与降水、径流并列的项。

abstract.en: Picture two invisible plumes, one from bare soil and one from leaf pores, meeting above the field.
abstract.cn: 想象两股看不见的气流，一股来自裸露土面，一股来自叶孔，在田地上空汇合。

abstract.en: Picture a bank account drained by thousands of tiny unnoticeable withdrawals.
abstract.cn: 想象一个账户被成千上万笔难以察觉的小额支取慢慢掏空。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the heat itself escapes as the water leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，水离开的同时把热量也一并带走。

examples.en: Warm, dry air raises evapotranspiration across the whole basin.
examples.cn: 温暖干燥的空气抬高了整个流域的蒸散。

examples.en: The model separates evaporation from transpiration instead of treating evapotranspiration as one number.
examples.cn: 该模型把蒸发与蒸腾分开，而不是把蒸散当作一个数处理。

examples.en: Loss of vegetation reduced evapotranspiration and changed the regional rainfall pattern.
examples.cn: 植被减少降低了蒸散，改变了区域降水格局。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）+ vapor（蒸汽）+ trans（穿过）+ spir（呼吸）+ ation」——土面吐汽、叶片呼气，合成蒸散

root: 拉丁 e-（向外）+ vapor「蒸汽」+ trans-（穿过）+ spirare「呼吸」+ -ation；vapor 与 spirare 的更深来源均不确定，整个复合词是近代水文学与农学合成的术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one invisible current: water leaves the ground by two routes, is added into a single flux, is measured as a depth, becomes a farm demand, an accounting term, a heat channel, an ecological loss and finally a metaphor for quiet drainage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一股看不见的水流展开：水经两条路线离地，合成一股通量，被量成水深，成为农田需求、核算项、热量通道、生态损失，最后成为「悄然流失」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two unseen plumes of vapour, one from soil and one from leaves, rise and merge over a field.
core.cn: 核心意象：两股看不见的水汽，一股来自土面，一股来自叶片，在田地上空升起并汇合。

branches.en: TWO CHANNELS: the whole flux and its plant half are the same current seen together or apart.
branches.cn: 两条通道：整体通量与其中的植物部分，是同一股水流的合看与分看。

branches.en: ACCOUNTING: the event becomes a depth of water and a line in the catchment budget.
branches.cn: 核算：事件变成水深数字，变成流域收支表上的一行。

branches.en: FARM DEMAND: what leaves must be replaced, so the flux turns into an irrigation requirement.
branches.cn: 农田需求：失去的必须补回，于是通量变成灌溉要求。

branches.en: TWO LANGUAGES: energy units read the same flux as latent heat, ecology reads it as lost streamflow.
branches.cn: 两套语言：能量单位把同一股通量读作潜热，生态学把它读作失去的径流。

branches.en: METAPHOR: valuable things leave through many small openings, as water leaves a field.
branches.cn: 比喻：有价值之物经许多小口离去，正如水离开田地。

intro.en: Evapotranspiration is a compound of two Latin-derived nouns, so it can be read morpheme by morpheme across four Latin elements and two English suffixes.
intro.cn: evapotranspiration 由两个拉丁来源名词合成，因此可以沿四个拉丁成分与两个英语后缀逐语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin vapor gives vapor, vaporous and vaporize; Latin spirare gives transpire, perspire, inspire and respiration; e- and trans- supply the directions 'out' and 'through'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vapor 衍生 vapor、vaporous 与 vaporize；拉丁 spirare 衍生 transpire、perspire、inspire 与 respiration；e- 与 trans- 提供「向外」与「穿过」两个方向。

items.example: The prefix marks vapour leaving the surface.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出水汽离开地表。

items.example: Vapor rose from the warm asphalt.
items.exampleCN: 水汽从发烫的柏油路面升起。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing
items.example: Evaporation dried the pan in an hour.
items.exampleCN: 蒸发在一小时内把盘子烤干。

items.example: The prefix marks vapour passing through leaf surfaces.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出水汽穿过叶片表面。

items.example: The root carries the image of breathing out.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「呼出气」的意象。

items.meaning: the act of turning to vapour
items.example: Evaporation from the reservoir peaked in July.
items.exampleCN: 水库蒸发量在七月达到高峰。

items.example: Transpiration cools a leaf in strong sun.
items.exampleCN: 烈日下蒸腾为叶片降温。

items.example: Perspiration soaked his collar.
items.exampleCN: 汗水浸湿了他的衣领。

items.meaning: to lose water by both channels
items.example: The canopy evapotranspires most of the summer rain.
items.exampleCN: 冠层把夏季雨水的大部分蒸散掉。

items.meaningCN: 以蒸散量为计算依据的
items.example: They used an evapotranspiration-based schedule.
items.exampleCN: 他们采用了以蒸散量为依据的灌溉计划。

definition_zh: 水资源保护；节水；通过减少浪费与提高效率来保护水资源的行为与做法
definition_en: the practice and policy of using water carefully so that waste is cut and supplies last for present and future needs
core_image: 一只滴水的水龙头被拧紧，水表上的指针随之慢下来，屋外的水库因此多留下一层水面
scene: 北方城市的社区活动上，志愿者教居民给洗手池换上节水龙头。Water conservation begins with fixing a single leaking tap.
sceneCN: 这里 water conservation 指「家庭与社区层面减少用水浪费的具体做法」（第 3 个义项：更换器具、修补渗漏等日常节水措施）；句意为节水从修好一个漏水龙头开始。图中可辨识物件：洗手池、节水龙头、扳手、水表。

pos.zh: 水资源保护；节水（不可数名词短语）

senses.title: Careful use so that water is not wasted
senses.titleCN: 节约用水，减少浪费
senses.definition: the general practice of using water economically so that none is lost unnecessarily
senses.definitionCN: 总体上经济地用水，使水不被无谓流失的做法
senses.example: Water conservation begins with fixing a single leaking tap.
senses.exampleCN: 节水从修好一个漏水龙头开始。
senses.why: Conservation is built on conservare 'to keep safe', so the phrase names keeping a supply safe by not throwing any of it away.
senses.whyCN: conservation 出自 conservare「守住」，因此这个短语指「不把水白白扔掉」来守住储备。

senses.title: Demand management as public policy
senses.titleCN: 作为公共政策的需求管理
senses.definition: the set of rules, prices and programmes by which an authority reduces demand instead of building new supply
senses.definitionCN: 主管机构通过规则、价格与项目压低需求、而非新建供水的一整套办法
senses.example: The city made water conservation the first line of its drought plan.
senses.exampleCN: 该市把节水作为抗旱计划的第一道防线。
senses.why: Once saving a resource becomes a government task, the phrase shifts from household habit to the policy that shapes it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦节约资源成为政府任务，这个短语就从家庭习惯转为塑造习惯的政策。

senses.title: Household and community measures
senses.titleCN: 家庭与社区层面的具体措施
senses.definition: everyday steps such as low-flow fixtures, leak repair, shorter showers and rainwater collection
senses.definitionCN: 低流量器具、修补渗漏、缩短淋浴与收集雨水等日常做法
senses.example: Water conservation in the building cut its bill by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼的节水措施让水费降了三分之一。
senses.why: Policy reaches people as hardware and habit, and this sense names the taps, tanks and timers that carry the idea.
senses.whyCN: 政策以器具和习惯的形式落到人身上，这个义项就指落实这一理念的龙头、水箱与定时器。

senses.title: Irrigation efficiency on farms
senses.titleCN: 农业灌溉中的用水效率
senses.definition: field practices that deliver water to crops with less evaporation, seepage and runoff loss
senses.definitionCN: 减少蒸发、渗漏与径流损失，把水送到作物根部的田间做法
senses.example: Drip lines brought water conservation to the orange groves.
senses.exampleCN: 滴灌带把节水带进了柑橘园。
senses.why: Agriculture takes most of the world's water, so the phrase's largest practical sense is the efficiency of the ditch and the sprinkler.
senses.whyCN: 农业取走世界上大部分水，因此这个短语最大的实用义项就是水渠与喷灌的效率。

senses.title: Industrial reuse and recycling
senses.titleCN: 工业用水回用与循环
senses.definition: closed-loop practices in which process water is cleaned and used again rather than discharged
senses.definitionCN: 把工艺用水净化后再次使用、而非直接排放的闭路做法
senses.example: Cooling towers achieved water conservation by cycling the same volume.
senses.exampleCN: 冷却塔靠循环同一批水量实现节水。
senses.why: For a factory the saving is not less use but repeated use, and the phrase covers that loop as well.
senses.whyCN: 对工厂来说，节约不是少用而是反复用，这个短语也涵盖这一循环。

senses.title: Protecting the source and its flows
senses.titleCN: 保护水源与生态流量
senses.definition: leaving enough water in rivers, lakes and aquifers to keep ecosystems and downstream users supplied
senses.definitionCN: 在河流、湖泊与含水层中留足水量，以维持生态与下游用水
senses.example: Water conservation also means leaving the river its summer flow.
senses.exampleCN: 节水也意味着给河流留下夏季流量。
senses.why: The oldest sense of conserving is keeping a thing intact; applied to a river, it means not emptying it.
senses.whyCN: conserving 最古老的意义是保持完整；用在河流上，就是不要把它抽空。

senses.title: Storage that keeps water for later
senses.titleCN: 把水存起来留待后用
senses.definition: tanks, reservoirs and managed aquifer recharge that hold water through dry periods
senses.definitionCN: 水箱、水库与含水层回补，把水存过干旱期
senses.example: Roof tanks gave the village water conservation through the dry months.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶水箱让村子在旱月里也能存住水。
senses.why: Keeping water safe includes keeping it somewhere, so storage belongs to the same family of meanings as not wasting it.
senses.whyCN: 把水守住也包括把水存放在某处，因此蓄水与「不浪费」属于同一族含义。

senses.title: Abstract: prudent use of any shared resource
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：像省水一样节制使用共有资源
senses.definition: a transferred use for careful, sparing management of any limited shared resource
senses.definitionCN: 转指对任何有限共有资源进行细心、节制管理
senses.example: The team applied water conservation habits to its own meeting time.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团队把节水的习惯用到自己的会议时间上。
senses.why: The metaphor survives because the shape is general: a finite pool, many users, and a rule against waste.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻能成立，是因为形态是通用的：有限的池子、许多使用者，以及一条不许浪费的规矩。

intro.en: Water conservation joins the native English word water to a Latin-derived noun of keeping safe. The phrase itself is a modern English construction, transparent in meaning. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: water conservation 把英语本族词 water 与拉丁来源的「守住」名词连在一起。这个短语本身是近代英语构造，含义透明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Wæter is the native word for water, recorded from the earliest English. Its deeper origin is not established; the common Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: wæter 是英语最早期就有记录的本族「水」词。其更深来源未得到证明；常为它提出的印欧形式是重构，而非有书证的词。

items.en: Servare meant 'to keep, watch over, guard'. Its own deeper origin is unsettled; the link sometimes drawn to servire 'to serve' is a hypothesis rather than a proven derivation.
items.cn: servare 意为「看守、保存、守护」。其更深来源无定论；有人把它与 servire「服侍」联系起来，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Com- 'thoroughly, together' plus servare produced conservare 'to keep safe, maintain'; the noun conservatio named the act.
items.cn: com-「彻底、共同」加 servare 构成 conservare「保住、维持」；名词 conservatio 指这一动作。

items.en: Old French conserver brought the verb into English in the fourteenth century, and conservation first named the preserving of health, goods or rights.
items.cn: 古法语 conserver 在十四世纪把动词带入英语，conservation 最初指对健康、财物或权利的保全。

items.en: Water and conservation were joined in English writing on resource management, first for forests and soils and then for rivers and city supply.
items.cn: water 与 conservation 在英语资源管理写作中连用，先用于森林与土壤，后用于河流与城市供水。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date of the compound, deeper origin of wæter and servare): no single earliest citation is fixed for the phrase, so its first date is approximate; the pre-English origin of wæter and the pre-Latin origin of servare are unsettled, and any forms offered for them are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（该短语的首见年代，以及 wæter 与 servare 的更深词源）：这个短语没有公认的最早书证，首见年代只能约计；wæter 在英语之前的来源与 servare 在拉丁语之前的来源均无定论，凡为其提出的形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds phrases built on conserve or on the word water that name neighbouring but distinct ideas; group two holds terms from water management that are regularly substituted for this one.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 conserve 或同含 water、但所指相邻而不同的短语；第二组是水管理领域中常被拿来替换本短语的术语。

entries.definition: The ratio of useful water delivered to water taken; it is a performance figure, while conservation is the wider practice that aims at it.
entries.definitionCN: 有效供水与取水之比；它是一个绩效数字，而 conservation 是追求这一数字的更宽泛做法。

entries.definition: The plain everyday phrase for using less water, usually of devices and habits rather than of policy.
entries.definitionCN: 指少用水的日常说法，通常用于器具与习惯，而不用于政策。

entries.definition: Keeping water fit to use, as in stored samples; preservation guards quality, while conservation guards quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 保持水可使用，如保存水样；preservation 护的是质量，conservation 护的是数量。

entries.definition: Protection of soil from erosion and loss; the construction is identical but the resource is different.
entries.definitionCN: 保护土壤不受侵蚀与流失；构造完全相同，但所护资源不同。

entries.definition: The utility's term for reducing consumption by pricing, rules and retrofits; water conservation is the public-facing name for the same effort.
entries.definitionCN: 供水机构对通过价格、规则与改造压低用水的称呼；water conservation 是同一努力面向公众的名字。

entries.definition: Sending treated water back into a second use; it is one method within conservation rather than the whole policy.
entries.definitionCN: 把处理过的水送入第二次用途；它是节水中的一种方法，而非整套政策。

entries.definition: Repeated use of the same water in a process; it overlaps with conservation but stresses the loop rather than the saving.
entries.definitionCN: 同一批水在工艺中反复使用；它与节水重叠，但强调循环而非节约。

entries.definition: The general protection of any resource; the phrase simply fixes that noun to water.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指对任何资源的保护；本短语只是把这个名词限定到水。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Conservation is com- 'thoroughly' plus servare 'keep safe': keeping a supply safe all round.
normal.cn: conservation 是 com-「彻底」加 servare「守住」：把储备整个护住。

normal.en: The phrase is simply conservation applied to water, as soil conservation applies it to soil.
normal.cn: 这个短语就是把 conservation 用在水上，正如 soil conservation 用在土上。

normal.en: The family runs conserve, conservation, conservationist, conservative and conservancy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 conserve、conservation、conservationist、conservative 与 conservancy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the practice: water conservation measures, water conservation program, household water conservation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出做法：节水措施、节水计划、家庭节水。

normal.en: The everyday counterpart is written as a compound adjective: water-saving taps, water-conservation technology.
normal.cn: 日常对应说法写作复合形容词：节水龙头、节水技术。

abstract.en: Picture a tap turned just past the drip, and a reservoir that keeps one extra layer of water.
abstract.cn: 想象水龙头被拧过滴水的位置，水库因此多留了一层水面。

abstract.en: Picture a shared jug at a table where everyone pours a little less.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上共用的水壶，每个人都少倒一点。

abstract.en: Picture a budget in which saving is not a loss but a reserve kept for a dry day.
abstract.cn: 想象一本预算，省下的不是损失，而是留给旱日的储备。

examples.en: Water conservation measures cut the city's demand by nearly a fifth.
examples.cn: 节水措施把全市用水需求削减了近五分之一。

examples.en: Farmers turned to water conservation when the wells began to fail.
examples.cn: 水井开始枯竭时，农民转向节水。

examples.en: The school runs a water conservation campaign every spring.
examples.cn: 这所学校每年春天开展节水宣传。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「water（水）+ conservation（保护）」——把水守住，别让它白白流走 → 节水、水资源保护

root: 英语复合短语：water 来自古英语 wæter「水」，更深来源不确定；conservation 来自拉丁 conservare「保住、维持」= com-（彻底）+ servare「守住」，servare 更深来源亦无定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one rule: take less, lose less, use it again, keep the source full and store what is spared. The last sense applies that rule to any shared pool.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条规则展开：少取、少漏、再用、让水源保持充盈、把省下的存起来。最后一个义项把这条规则用到任何共用的池子上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dripping tap is closed and the level in the reservoir stops falling.
core.cn: 核心意象：滴水龙头被拧紧，水库的水位不再下降。

branches.en: SAVING: personal habit and public policy are the same rule at two scales.
branches.cn: 节约：个人习惯与公共政策是同一条规则在两个尺度上。

branches.en: DEVICES AND FIELDS: taps, showers, drip lines and schedules all deliver the saving.
branches.cn: 器具与田间：龙头、淋浴、滴灌带与灌溉安排都在落实节约。

branches.en: LOOP: industry saves by using the same water twice rather than by using less.
branches.cn: 循环：工业靠同一批水用两次来节约，而不是靠少用。

branches.en: KEEPING INTACT: a river left with its flow and a tank kept full are both stores held safe.
branches.cn: 保持完整：给河流留流量、把水箱存满，都是把储备守住。

branches.en: TRANSFER: any finite shared pool can be managed by the same rule.
branches.cn: 转移：任何有限的共有池子都能用同一条规则管理。

intro.en: The phrase combines a native English noun with a Latin-derived noun of two morphemes, so it can be read as an English compound and as a Latin family.
intro.cn: 这个短语由英语本族名词与一个含两个语素的拉丁来源名词构成，因此既可当作英语复合词读，也可当作一个拉丁词族读。

latinIntro.en: Latin servare gives conserve, conservation, conservator, preserve, reserve and observe; com- adds 'thoroughly, together'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 servare 衍生 conserve、conservation、conservator、preserve、reserve 与 observe；com- 增添「彻底、共同」。

items.example: The water in the tank lasted all summer.
items.exampleCN: 水箱里的水撑过了整个夏天。

items.example: The prefix binds the keeping into one whole act.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「守住」收束为一个整体动作。

items.structure: servare, servavi, servatum (Latin verb, 'to keep, guard')
items.example: The root carries the idea of keeping watch.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「看守」的意思。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing
items.example: The conservation of the old mill took years.
items.exampleCN: 这座老磨坊的保护工作花了多年。

items.example: Soil conservation slowed the gully.
items.exampleCN: 土壤保护减缓了沟蚀。

items.meaning: to keep safe; to use sparingly
items.example: They conserve water in the dry season.
items.exampleCN: 他们在旱季节约用水。

items.meaning: tending to keep things as they are
items.meaningCN: 倾向维持原状的；保守的
items.example: She gave a conservative estimate.
items.exampleCN: 她给出了保守的估计。

items.meaning: a person who works to protect nature
items.example: The conservationist mapped the springs.
items.exampleCN: 这位保护者标出了泉眼位置。

items.example: Water-saving taps cut the bill.
items.exampleCN: 节水龙头降低了水费。

items.example: The water-conservation plan was approved.
items.exampleCN: 节水计划获得批准。

definition_zh: 水资源；可供利用的水源与水量
definition_en: a body or supply of water that is available, or can be made available, for human use and for ecosystems
core_image: 山脚的一条河与一口井在管理图上被圈成两块，旁边写着可供取用的水量
scene: 山脚下的村庄靠一条河与一口井取水，管水员在地图上圈出可用的范围。The village counts the river as its main water resource.
sceneCN: 这里 water resource 指「一个地方可供取用的水源与水量」（第 1 个义项：能持续供给使用的天然水体）；句意为这个村子把这条河当成本地主要的水资源。图中可辨识物件：河流、井口、管理地图、圈注线。

pos.zh: 水资源；水源（常用复数 water resources 表示一地的水资源总量）

derivatives.zh: 足智多谋的；善于动用资源的

senses.title: Water available for use in a place
senses.titleCN: 一地可供使用的水
senses.definition: the water naturally present in a region that people can draw on for households, farms and industry
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区天然存在、可供家庭、农业与工业取用的水
senses.example: The village counts the river as its main water resource.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子把这条河当成本地主要的水资源。
senses.why: Resource comes from Latin resurgere 'to rise again', the image of a spring welling up, so water resource is literally a water source that keeps supplying.
senses.whyCN: resource 出自拉丁 resurgere「重新涌起」，是泉水上涌的意象，因此 water resource 字面上就是「会持续供给的水源」。

senses.title: A named body of water as a source
senses.titleCN: 作为取水源头的具体水体
senses.definition: a particular river, lake, reservoir or aquifer treated as a unit of supply
senses.definitionCN: 被当作一个供水单元的具体河流、湖泊、水库或含水层
senses.example: The reservoir is the city's largest surface water resource.
senses.exampleCN: 这座水库是该市最大的地表水源。
senses.why: Planning needs countable units, so the abstract supply is broken into named bodies that can be mapped and allocated.
senses.whyCN: 规划需要可数的单位，于是抽象的水量被分成可以上图、可以分配的具名水体。

senses.title: Renewable versus non-renewable supply
senses.titleCN: 可再生与不可再生的分类
senses.definition: the classification of a supply by whether rain and inflow replace what is taken
senses.definitionCN: 按降雨与来水能否补足取用量对水源所作的分类
senses.example: Deep fossil aquifers are a non-renewable water resource.
senses.exampleCN: 深层化石含水层是不可再生的水资源。
senses.why: The resource frame borrowed from mining and forestry, where the key question is whether the stock refills.
senses.whyCN: resource 这一框架借自矿业与林业，其中最要紧的问题就是储量会不会补回。

senses.title: An economic input with a value
senses.titleCN: 具有价值的经济投入要素
senses.definition: water treated as a natural asset that can be priced, traded and counted in national accounts
senses.definitionCN: 把水当作可定价、可交易、可计入国民账户的自然资源资产
senses.example: The report valued the aquifer as a national water resource.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把该含水层估作一项国家水资源资产。
senses.why: Economics turns a physical supply into an asset, so the phrase acquires the sense of capital rather than flow.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把物理供给变成资产，这个短语于是带上「资本」而非「流量」的意思。

senses.title: Dependable yield and storage capacity
senses.titleCN: 可靠供水量与蓄水能力
senses.definition: the volume an engineer can guarantee in a dry year, including what dams and tanks hold
senses.definitionCN: 工程师在干旱年份能够保证供应的水量，含水库与水箱的蓄量
senses.example: The dam raised the region's dependable water resource by half.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝把该地区的可靠供水量提高了一半。
senses.why: Engineering cares about the worst year, so the resource is defined by the yield that can be relied on, not by the average.
senses.whyCN: 工程关心的是最差的年份，因此水资源以「能依靠的产量」来定义，而不是以平均值。

senses.title: A legal entitlement to take water
senses.titleCN: 法律上的取水权与配水份额
senses.definition: a recognised right or allocation to divert or pump a stated volume
senses.definitionCN: 被承认的、可引取或抽取一定水量的权利或配额
senses.example: The tribe holds a senior water resource right on that creek.
senses.exampleCN: 该部落在那条溪上持有优先取水权。
senses.why: Once water is scarce, the resource is defined by who may take it, so the phrase shifts from water to entitlement.
senses.whyCN: 水一旦稀缺，资源就由「谁可以取」来界定，这个短语于是从水转向权利。

senses.title: A shared resource across borders
senses.titleCN: 跨国共享的水资源
senses.definition: a supply lying in more than one jurisdiction, where use by one party affects another
senses.definitionCN: 位于不止一个辖区、一方使用会影响另一方的水源
senses.example: The two states negotiated a treaty over their shared water resource.
senses.exampleCN: 两州就共享水资源谈判达成条约。
senses.why: The same body of water becomes political when upstream use changes what downstream users receive.
senses.whyCN: 当上游取用改变了下游所得，同一片水就成了政治问题。

senses.title: Water as amenity and cultural value
senses.titleCN: 作为景观与文化价值的水
senses.definition: the recreational, aesthetic and cultural worth of a water body, counted alongside its volume
senses.definitionCN: 水体在休闲、审美与文化上的价值，与它的水量一并计算
senses.example: Residents defended the lake as a water resource for the whole town.
senses.exampleCN: 居民把这片湖当作全城的资源来维护。
senses.why: The resource frame widened beyond litres to include everything a community draws from a water body, including beauty and recreation.
senses.whyCN: resource 这一框架从升数扩展开来，纳入社区从水体取得的一切，包括美景与休闲。

intro.en: Water resource combines the native English word for water with a French-Latin noun for a source that rises again. The phrase is modern and transparent. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: water resource 把英语本族的「水」词与一个法拉丁来源的「重新涌起之源」名词连在一起。这个短语是近代的，构词透明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Wæter is the earliest English word for water. Its deeper origin is not established; the common Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: wæter 是英语最早的「水」词。其更深来源未得到证明；常为它提出的印欧形式是重构，而非有记录的词。

items.en: Ressource meant 'a source, a spring', from resourdre 'to rise again'. The image is water welling back up after being drawn down.
items.cn: ressource 意为「源头、泉」，出自 resourdre「重新涌起」。意象是被取用之后又涌回的水。

items.en: Re- 'again' plus surgere 'to rise' produced resurgere 'to rise again'; surgere is sub- 'from below' plus regere 'to lead straight, guide'.
items.cn: re-「再」加 surgere「升起」构成 resurgere「重新涌起」；surgere 则是 sub-「从下」加 regere「引直、引导」。

items.en: English resource first meant 'a means of supplying a want', then any stock of useful material, and only later the natural supplies of a country.
items.cn: 英语 resource 最初指「补足所需的手段」，随后指任何有用物资的储备，再往后才指一国的自然资源。

items.en: Water and resource were joined in engineering and planning writing when supply had to be counted, allocated and stored.
items.cn: 当供水需要计量、分配与蓄存时，water 与 resource 在工程与规划写作中连用。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date of the compound only): the phrase has no fixed earliest citation, so its first date is approximate; the pre-English origin of wæter is unsettled and any form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅该短语的首见年代）：这个短语没有固定的最早书证，首见年代只能约计；wæter 在英语之前的来源无定论，凡为其提出的形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds water compounds that look alike but name a point, a delivery system, a kept volume or a channel; group two holds technical terms from hydrology and economics that overlap with this phrase.
note.cn: 第一组是同含 water、外形相近，但分别指取水点、输配系统、存留水量或水道；第二组是水文学与经济学中与本短语重叠的技术术语。

entries.definition: The specific place water comes from, such as a spring or intake; it is one point within a water resource, not the whole supply.
entries.definitionCN: 水具体来自的地点，如泉眼或取水口；它是水资源中的一个点，不是全部供给。

entries.definition: The system and service that delivers water to users; it is infrastructure built on a resource rather than the resource itself.
entries.definitionCN: 把水送到用户的系统与服务；它建在水资源之上的设施，而非资源本身。

entries.definition: Water held back deliberately for later or for emergency, a stored portion rather than the total available.
entries.definitionCN: 有意留存备后用或应急的水，是总可用量中的一部分。

entries.definition: The bed and banks along which water flows; it names the channel, not the volume it carries.
entries.definitionCN: 水流经过的河床与河岸；它指通道，而非所携水量。

entries.definition: Water with little dissolved salt; it is a quality class that may or may not be a usable resource.
entries.definitionCN: 溶解盐很少的水；它是按品质划分的一类，未必都能成为可用资源。

entries.definition: A rock layer that holds and transmits groundwater; it is one kind of water resource, not the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 储存并输送地下水的岩层；它是水资源的一种，而非总称。

entries.definition: The land area draining into one river system; it is the unit within which a water resource is counted.
entries.definitionCN: 汇入同一河系的陆地区域；它是在其中核算水资源的单元。

entries.definition: The stock of natural assets treated as capital; water resource is one entry in that stock.
entries.definitionCN: 被当作资本的自然资产存量；水资源是其中一项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Resource is re- 'again' plus surgere 'to rise': a spring that keeps rising is a resource.
normal.cn: resource 是 re-「再」加 surgere「升起」：不断涌起的泉就是资源。

normal.en: The phrase is conservation applied to supply: what can be drawn on without being destroyed.
normal.cn: 这个短语就是可被取用而不被毁掉的供给。

normal.en: The family runs resource, resourceful, resourcefulness, resourcing and water-resource.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 resource、resourceful、resourcefulness、resourcing 与 water-resource。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark planning: water resource management, water resources planning, shared water resources.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出规划语境：水资源管理、水资源规划、共享水资源。

normal.en: The plural water resources is the usual form for a region's total supply.
normal.cn: 复数 water resources 是表示一地区水资源总量的常用形式。

abstract.en: Picture a spring that refills itself overnight after every bucket taken.
abstract.cn: 想象一眼泉，每次取走一桶，夜里又自己补满。

abstract.en: Picture a map with two circles on it, and a number written beside each circle.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上画了两个圈，每个圈旁写着一个数。

abstract.en: Picture a shared well on a border, with two villages drawing from the same rope.
abstract.cn: 想象边境上一口共用的井，两个村子拉着同一根井绳。

examples.en: The basin's water resources are already fully allocated.
examples.cn: 该流域的水资源已全部分配完毕。

examples.en: Groundwater is a hidden water resource that responds slowly to policy.
examples.cn: 地下水是一种隐蔽的水资源，对政策反应缓慢。

examples.en: Cities must protect the water resource before expanding supply.
examples.cn: 城市必须先保护水源，再扩大供水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「water（水）+ resource（资源）」——可以不断取用的水源 → 水资源

root: 英语复合短语：water 来自古英语 wæter「水」，更深来源不确定；resource 经古法语 ressource「源头、泉」出自拉丁 resurgere「重新涌起」= re-（再）+ surgere「升起」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one supply: water present in a place, a named body, a renewable or finite stock, an asset, a guaranteed yield, a legal share, a shared border supply and finally an amenity a community values.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一份供给展开：一地存在的水、具名的水体、可再生或有限的储量、一项资产、可保证的产量、一份法定份额、跨境共享的供给，最后是社区珍视的景观价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a river and a well circled on a management map, each with a usable volume written beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：管理地图上圈出的河与井，旁边各写着可供取用的水量。

branches.en: SUPPLY: the total available and each mapped body are the same provision at two scales.
branches.cn: 供给：总可用量与每个上图水体，是同一份供给在两个尺度上。

branches.en: REFILL: renewable or fossil, the decisive question is whether the stock comes back.
branches.cn: 回补：无论可再生还是化石水，关键都在于储量会不会回来。

branches.en: VALUE AND YIELD: economics calls it capital, engineering calls it dependable yield.
branches.cn: 价值与产量：经济学称之为资本，工程学称之为可靠产量。

branches.en: ENTITLEMENT: a right held by one user and a treaty between states are both shares.
branches.cn: 权利：一户持有的取水权与国家间的条约，都是份额。

branches.en: AMENITY: what a community draws from water includes beauty and recreation.
branches.cn: 景观：社区从水中取得的还包括美景与休闲。

intro.en: The phrase joins a native English noun to a Latin-derived noun that splits into a prefix, a root and a suffix, so both an English and a Latin reading are possible.
intro.cn: 这个短语把英语本族名词连到一个拉丁来源名词上，后者可拆成前缀、词根与后缀，因此既能按英语读，也能按拉丁语素读。

latinIntro.en: Latin surgere gives resource, resurge, insurgent and surge; re- adds 'again' and sub- 'from below'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 surgere 衍生 resource、resurge、insurgent 与 surge；re- 添「再」，sub- 添「从下」。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着水向上涌的意象。

items.exampleCN: 重新涌起的泉水灌满了池塘。

definition_zh: 水资源短缺；缺水；可用水量不足以满足需求的状况
definition_en: the condition in which the water available in a place falls short of what households, farms, industry and ecosystems require
core_image: 干涸的井口边排着一列水桶，桶底只刮到一层湿泥
scene: 旱季的村子里，人们在见底的井边排队等水，桶里只舀起一层泥浆。Water scarcity turned a routine chore into a daily negotiation.
sceneCN: 这里 water scarcity 指「可用水量低于需求的缺水状况」（第 1 个义项：天然来水与取用量之间的实物缺口）；句意为缺水把日常家务变成每天的讨价还价。图中可辨识物件：干井、水桶、排队的人、泥浆。

pos.zh: 水资源短缺；缺水（不可数名词短语，也作 water scarcities 表示多地的缺水情形）

senses.title: Physical shortfall of water against demand
senses.titleCN: 来水不足以满足需求的实物缺口
senses.definition: the condition in which a region's natural supply cannot meet the water its users need
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区的天然供水无法满足其使用者所需水量的状况
senses.example: Water scarcity turned a routine chore into a daily negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 缺水把日常家务变成每天的讨价还价。
senses.why: Scarcity names a gap, not a total: the word only appears when demand presses against a supply that cannot grow.
senses.whyCN: scarcity 命名的是一个缺口而非总量：只有当需求逼住无法增长的供给时，这个词才出现。

senses.title: Economic scarcity from missing infrastructure
senses.titleCN: 因缺少水利设施造成的经济性缺水
senses.definition: shortage caused not by absent water but by the lack of wells, pipes, pumps and money to deliver it
senses.definitionCN: 并非没有水，而是缺少井、管道、水泵与资金把水送到的短缺
senses.example: The district suffers economic water scarcity despite a full river.
senses.exampleCN: 这个区虽有满河的流水，却仍在经济性缺水之中。
senses.why: Development economists split the idea in two, because a place can be dry by poverty rather than by climate.
senses.whyCN: 发展经济学家把这个概念一分为二，因为一个地方可能因贫困而非因气候而干涸。

senses.title: A measured index per person
senses.titleCN: 按人均水量计算的量化指标
senses.definition: the condition classified by renewable water available per person per year against agreed thresholds
senses.definitionCN: 以每年人均可再生水量对照公认阈值所作的缺水分类
senses.example: The country crossed into absolute water scarcity last decade.
senses.exampleCN: 该国在上一个十年进入了绝对缺水区间。
senses.why: Policy needs a line to cross, so the shortage becomes a number that can be compared between countries.
senses.whyCN: 政策需要一条可越过的界线，于是短缺变成可在国家间比较的数字。

senses.title: Seasonal or intermittent shortage
senses.titleCN: 季节性、间歇性的缺水
senses.definition: a shortage that arrives with the dry season, the failure of monsoon rain or a shift in snowmelt
senses.definitionCN: 随旱季、季风降雨失败或融雪改变而来的短缺
senses.example: Seasonal water scarcity empties the upland villages each March.
senses.exampleCN: 季节性缺水每年三月让高地上的村子空掉。
senses.why: A supply can be adequate over a year and still fail in the weeks when nothing falls.
senses.whyCN: 按年计算足够的水，仍可能在滴雨不下的那几周里断掉。

senses.title: Farm-level shortage that threatens food
senses.titleCN: 威胁粮食生产的农田缺水
senses.definition: the shortage that forces irrigation to be cut, yields to fall and cropping patterns to change
senses.definitionCN: 迫使灌溉削减、产量下降、种植结构改变的缺水
senses.example: Water scarcity forced the valley to abandon its thirsty crop.
senses.exampleCN: 缺水迫使这个河谷放弃了耗水的作物。
senses.why: Because irrigation takes the largest share, scarcity is usually felt first in the field and then at the table.
senses.whyCN: 由于灌溉占最大份额，缺水通常先在田里被感到，然后才到餐桌上。

senses.title: Urban competition and rationing
senses.titleCN: 城市里各用户争水与配给
senses.definition: the shortage that sets households, industry and farms against one another and brings cuts and rationing
senses.definitionCN: 使家庭、工业与农业彼此争水，并带来限水与配给的短缺
senses.example: Water scarcity split the city into supply zones with different hours.
senses.exampleCN: 缺水把这座城市划成供水时段不同的若干区。
senses.why: When a fixed volume meets many claimants, shortage becomes an allocation problem rather than a physical one.
senses.whyCN: 当固定水量面对众多索取者，短缺就成了分配问题而非物理问题。

senses.title: Institutional scarcity: weak governance
senses.titleCN: 制度层面的缺水：管理能力不足
senses.definition: the shortage produced by missing data, unclear rights and agencies unable to enforce allocation
senses.definitionCN: 由数据缺失、权利不清与机构无力执行分配所造成的短缺
senses.example: Water scarcity persisted although the reservoir held enough.
senses.exampleCN: 水库的水还够，缺水却依旧持续。
senses.why: The scarcity literature added a third kind beyond physical and economic: the shortage made by institutions themselves.
senses.whyCN: 缺水研究在物理性与经济性之外加了第三种：由制度本身造成的短缺。

senses.title: Perceived shortage that changes behaviour
senses.titleCN: 感知上的短缺及其行为效应
senses.definition: a felt or anticipated shortage that makes people hoard, pay more or change what they grow
senses.definitionCN: 感到或预期到的短缺，使人囤积、多付钱或改变种植选择
senses.example: Water scarcity in the forecast drove up the price of pumps.
senses.exampleCN: 预报中的缺水推高了水泵价格。
senses.why: Scarcity can act before it arrives, because people respond to the expectation of a shortfall as strongly as to the shortfall itself.
senses.whyCN: 短缺可以在到来之前就起作用，因为人对缺口的预期，反应和对缺口本身一样强烈。

intro.en: Water scarcity joins the native word for water to a noun of shortage whose own derivation is disputed. The phrase itself is modern policy language. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: water scarcity 把本族的「水」词连到一个来源尚有争议的「短缺」名词上。这个短语本身是近代的政策语言。年代均为约数。

items.en: Wæter is the earliest English word for water. Its deeper origin is not established; the Indo-European form often proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: wæter 是英语最早的「水」词。其更深来源未得到证明；常为它提出的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: One account takes scarcity from Latin parcus 'sparing, frugal' through scarcitas. The deeper origin of parcus is uncertain, and the link sometimes suggested to parcere 'to spare' is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 一种说法认为 scarcity 经拉丁 scarcitas 出自 parcus「节省的、俭省的」。parcus 的更深来源不确定，有人把它与 parcere「节省」联系，那只是假说。

items.en: Another account connects the family to Vulgar Latin excarpsus 'plucked out', from ex- 'out' and carpere 'to pluck', the same source proposed for the adjective scarce. The two accounts are not reconciled.
items.cn: 另一种说法把这个词族连到俗拉丁 excarpsus「被摘出的」，出自 ex-「向外」与 carpere「摘取」，也就是形容词 scarce 被提出来的同一来源。两种说法尚未统一。

items.en: Old French scarcete meant 'smallness, scantiness, sparingness' and entered English in the fourteenth century as scarcity.
items.cn: 古法语 scarcete 意为「少、不足、俭省」，十四世纪以 scarcity 进入英语。

items.en: Water and scarcity were combined in development and hydrology writing once per-capita supply became a measured policy indicator.
items.cn: 当人均供水量成为可测的政策指标后，water 与 scarcity 在发展研究与水文学写作中连用。

items.en: Source uncertain (word root and first date): the derivation of scarcity is disputed between parcus and excarpsus, and no single earliest citation is fixed for the compound, so its first date is approximate; any older Indo-European forms offered for wæter are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：scarcity 的词源在 parcus 与 excarpsus 两种说法之间有争议，该复合词也没有公认的最早书证，首见年代只能约计；凡为 wæter 给出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds water phrases that look alike but name a dry spell, a stress measure or a calculated deficit; group two holds broader security and crisis terms that are often used in place of this phrase.
note.cn: 第一组是同含 water、外形相近，但分别指干旱时段、压力指标或计算出的缺口的短语；第二组是常被用来替换本短语的、更宽泛的安全与危机术语。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for not having enough water at a given moment; it is a temporary or local supply failure, while scarcity is a structural condition.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一时刻水不够用的日常说法；它是临时或局部的供应失败，而 scarcity 是结构性状况。

entries.definition: The share of renewable supply already withdrawn by users; it is an index, not the lived shortage itself.
entries.definitionCN: 可再生供水已被用户取走的比例；它是指标，而非实际感受到的短缺。

entries.definition: The gap between water needed and water supplied over a period, usually in millimetres or cubic metres.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间内需水与供水之间的缺口，通常以毫米或立方米计。

entries.definition: A prolonged period of unusually low rainfall; it is a climatic event that can produce water scarcity.
entries.definitionCN: 降雨异常偏少的持续时期；它是可能造成缺水的气候事件。

entries.definition: A scarcity severe enough to disrupt health, food or order; it adds an emergency to the shortage.
entries.definitionCN: 严重到破坏健康、粮食或秩序的短缺；它在短缺之上加了紧急状态。

entries.definition: The condition of having acceptable water for health and livelihoods; it is the goal whose failure is called scarcity.
entries.definitionCN: 为健康与生计提供可接受水量的状态；它是目标，其失败即被称为缺水。

entries.definition: A permanent climatic dryness; a desert is arid whether or not anyone demands water.
entries.definitionCN: 长期的气候干旱；无论有没有人取水，沙漠都是干旱的。

entries.definition: Any gap between what is supplied and what is required; water scarcity is this gap applied to water.
entries.definitionCN: 任何供给与需求之间的缺口；水资源短缺就是这个缺口用在水的身上。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Scarcity is the noun of scarce, and scarce describes what cannot be had in enough quantity.
normal.cn: scarcity 是 scarce 的名词，scarce 形容数量不够取用。

normal.en: The development split is fixed in two collocations: physical water scarcity and economic water scarcity.
normal.cn: 发展领域的划分固定在两对搭配里：物理性缺水与经济性缺水。

normal.en: The family runs scarcity, scarce, scarcely, scarceness and water-scarce.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 scarcity、scarce、scarcely、scarceness 与 water-scarce。

normal.en: The phrase sits beside shortage, stress and deficit: shortage is temporary, stress is a ratio, deficit is a calculated gap.
normal.cn: 这个短语与 shortage、stress、deficit 相邻：shortage 是临时的，stress 是比率，deficit 是算出来的缺口。

normal.en: Policy writes it as an index: absolute water scarcity, per-capita thresholds, water-scarcity risk.
normal.cn: 政策把它写成指标：绝对缺水、人均阈值、缺水风险。

abstract.en: Picture a queue at a well where the rope comes up with mud instead of water.
abstract.cn: 想象井边排队的人，井绳拉上来的是泥而不是水。

abstract.en: Picture a full river that cannot reach the houses because no pipe was ever laid.
abstract.cn: 想象一条满水的河，因为从未铺设管道而到不了人家。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour of shortage emptying the shelves before the shortage arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象短缺的传言在短缺到来之前就把货架清空。

examples.en: Water scarcity is measured per person, not per river.
examples.cn: 水资源短缺按人均衡量，而不是按河流衡量。

examples.en: Economic water scarcity can be relieved by building wells and pipes.
examples.cn: 经济性缺水可以通过打井和铺设管道来缓解。

examples.en: The report warned that water scarcity would reshape the region's farming.
examples.cn: 报告警告说，缺水将重塑该地区的农业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「water（水）+ scarcity（稀缺）」——水不够用 → 水资源短缺

root: 英语复合短语：water 来自古英语 wæter「水」，更深来源不确定；scarcity 经古法语 scarcete 出自拉丁 scarcitas，词根一说为 parcus「俭省的」，一说与俗拉丁 excarpsus「摘出的」相关，两说并列未定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gap: rain or supply falls short, demand presses in, the shortage is classified by cause, measured by index, felt by season, by field, by city, by institution and finally by expectation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个缺口展开：来水不足、需求逼近，短缺再按成因分类、按指标计量，并被季节、农田、城市、制度，最后是预期所感受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of buckets at a dry well, each scraping up mud.
core.cn: 核心意象：干井边排成一列的水桶，每只都只刮到泥。

branches.en: TWO CAUSES: water may be absent or simply undelivered, so the same gap has a physical and an economic face.
branches.cn: 两种成因：水可能真的没有，也可能只是没送到，同一个缺口有物理面与经济面。

branches.en: MEASURED AND SEASONAL: a threshold number and a dry season describe the same shortage at different scales.
branches.cn: 计量与季节：阈值数字与旱季描述的是同一短缺在不同尺度上的样子。

branches.en: FELT BY USERS: the field loses its crop and the city loses its hours of supply.
branches.cn: 使用者感受：农田失去作物，城市失去供水时段。

branches.en: MADE BY INSTITUTIONS: missing data and weak enforcement can hold a shortage in place.
branches.cn: 制度造成：数据缺失与执行不力可以让短缺一直维持。

branches.en: EXPECTED: a forecast shortfall moves prices and behaviour before any tap runs dry.
branches.cn: 预期：预报中的缺口在任何水龙头干之前就推动了价格与行为。

intro.en: The phrase joins a native English noun to a noun of shortage whose suffix and root are both debated, so the morpheme reading must be given with that caveat.
intro.cn: 这个短语把英语本族名词连到一个词根与后缀均有争议的「短缺」名词上，因此语素读法须带上这一保留。

latinIntro.en: Latin parcus 'sparing' would give scarcity through scarcitas; the rival account uses ex- 'out' plus carpere 'to pluck'; scarce, scarcity and scarceness all belong to this debated family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 parcus「俭省的」经由 scarcitas 可得 scarcity；对立说法用 ex-「向外」加 carpere「摘取」；scarce、scarcity 与 scarceness 都属这个有争议的词族。

items.exampleCN: 井里的水落到桶够不着的地方。

items.exampleCN: 俭省的人家很少浪费。

items.structure: Latin scarcitas via Old French scarcete

items.structure: Old French scars, of disputed origin

items.exampleCN: 那年夏天淡水稀少。

items.exampleCN: 他们勉强装满一桶。

items.example: The scarceness of rain shaped the harvest.
items.exampleCN: 雨水的稀少决定了收成。

items.exampleCN: 缺水地区进口粮食而不是水。

definition_zh: 短缺；稀缺；稀少；资源不足以满足需求的状态
definition_en: the state in which something needed exists in a quantity too small to satisfy the demand for it
core_image: 集市收摊时只剩最后一筐苹果，围上来的人却比开市时更多
scene: 集市收摊后，最后一筐苹果前反而围了更多人，摊主悄悄翻过价格牌。Scarcity pushed the price of the last basket higher than the first.
sceneCN: 这里 scarcity 指「物品稀少而需求仍在，因而产生溢价的情形」（第 9 个义项：因稀少而形成的附加价值）；句意为稀缺把最后一筐的价格抬得比第一筐还高。图中可辨识物件：空摊位、最后一筐苹果、围拢的人群、翻面的价牌。

pos.zh: 短缺；稀缺；稀少（可数指具体的一次短缺，不可数指普遍状态）

senses.title: A shortage of something needed
senses.titleCN: 所需之物的数量不足
senses.definition: the condition in which the supply of a needed thing is smaller than the amount people require
senses.definitionCN: 所需之物的供给小于人们所需数量的状况
senses.example: Scarcity of clean water shaped the town's history.
senses.exampleCN: 洁净水的短缺塑造了这座小镇的历史。
senses.why: Scarcity names a relationship, not a count: the same amount can be plentiful in one place and scarce in another because demand differs.
senses.whyCN: scarcity 命名的是关系而非数量：同样的量在一处充裕、在另一处稀缺，因为需求不同。

senses.title: Limited means against unlimited wants
senses.titleCN: 经济学：有限资源面对无限欲望
senses.definition: the founding condition of economics, in which resources are finite while human wants are not
senses.definitionCN: 经济学的出发点：资源有限而人的欲望无限
senses.example: Economics begins with scarcity and asks how to allocate.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学从稀缺出发，追问如何分配。
senses.why: Political economy took the everyday word and made it the reason markets and choices exist at all.
senses.whyCN: 政治经济学把这个日常词提升为市场与选择之所以存在的理由。

senses.title: The rarity of a particular object
senses.titleCN: 具体物品的稀有
senses.definition: the quality of being hard to find or obtain, as of a rare book or a scarce stamp
senses.definitionCN: 难以找到或取得的性质，如稀见书或罕邮票
senses.example: The scarcity of the first edition made it expensive.
senses.exampleCN: 初版书的稀有使它昂贵。
senses.why: Collectors use the word for the object itself, because what matters is how few survive rather than how many are wanted.
senses.whyCN: 收藏者用这个词指物本身，因为要紧的是存世多少，而不是多少人想要。

senses.title: Resource depletion in ecology
senses.titleCN: 生态学中的资源枯竭
senses.definition: the falling availability of a natural resource as it is used up or its habitat shrinks
senses.definitionCN: 自然资源因被耗尽或栖息地缩小而日益不可得
senses.example: Scarcity of nesting sites reduced the colony.
senses.exampleCN: 营巢地的稀缺使这个群落变小。
senses.why: Ecology views scarcity as a limit that shapes behaviour, competition and population size.
senses.whyCN: 生态学把稀缺看作塑造行为、竞争与种群规模的限制。

senses.title: Perceived scarcity and the mindset it creates
senses.titleCN: 感知到的稀缺及其心态
senses.definition: a felt shortage that narrows attention, encourages hoarding and pushes people toward short-term choices
senses.definitionCN: 感到的短缺，它会收窄注意力、促使人囤积并偏向短期选择
senses.example: A scarcity mindset kept the team from sharing information.
senses.exampleCN: 稀缺心态让这个团队不愿共享信息。
senses.why: Psychology separated the state from the perception, because people act on what they believe is scarce.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把状态与感知分开，因为人是按自己所相信的稀缺去行动的。

senses.title: Not enough hours in the day
senses.titleCN: 时间上的稀缺
senses.definition: the shortage of time relative to the tasks and commitments one has accepted
senses.definitionCN: 相对于已接受的任务与承诺而言的时间不足
senses.example: Time scarcity, not money, kept her from finishing the course.
senses.exampleCN: 让她没能修完课程的，是时间稀缺而非缺钱。
senses.why: The word extends easily to time, because hours are a fixed supply that cannot be increased by effort.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很容易延伸到时上，因为小时是固定供给，再努力也加不出来。

senses.title: Attention and information scarcity
senses.titleCN: 注意力与信息的稀缺
senses.definition: the shortage of attention available for a flood of information, or of reliable information itself
senses.definitionCN: 面对信息洪流时注意力的不足，或可靠信息本身的不足
senses.example: Information scarcity was replaced by information overload.
senses.exampleCN: 信息稀缺已被信息过载取代。
senses.why: Media economics applied the word to attention, since the scarce thing in an abundant market is the audience's focus.
senses.whyCN: 传媒经济学把这个词用到注意力上，因为在充裕的市场里，稀缺的是受众的专注。

senses.title: Artificial scarcity created on purpose
senses.titleCN: 为获利而人为制造的稀缺
senses.definition: a shortage deliberately maintained by a seller, cartel or platform to keep prices or status high
senses.definitionCN: 卖方、卡特尔或平台为维持高价或地位而有意保持的短缺
senses.example: The limited release was artificial scarcity, not a real shortfall.
senses.exampleCN: 限量发售是人为稀缺，并非真的缺货。
senses.why: Once scarcity can be manufactured, the word no longer assumes a natural limit; it can describe a strategy.
senses.whyCN: 一旦稀缺可以被制造，这个词就不再假定自然极限，而可以指一种策略。

senses.title: The premium that rarity adds to value
senses.titleCN: 因稀少而产生的价值溢价
senses.definition: the extra price or prestige an item gains because few like it are available
senses.definitionCN: 物品因同类稀少而获得的额外价格或声望
senses.example: Scarcity pushed the price of the last basket higher than the first.
senses.exampleCN: 稀缺把最后一筐的价格抬得比第一筐还高。
senses.why: Value can come from the supply side alone: when the same thing is abundant it is cheap, and when it is nearly gone it is dear.
senses.whyCN: 价值可以只来自供给一侧：同样的东西多时便宜，快没有时就贵。

intro.en: Scarcity came into English from Old French in the fourteenth century, but its deeper root is disputed between two accounts that are still taught side by side. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: scarcity 在十四世纪经古法语进入英语，但其更深词源在两种说法之间至今仍有争议，两种说法常并列讲授。年代均为约数。

items.en: One account derives scarcitas from parcus 'sparing, frugal'. The deeper origin of parcus is uncertain; the suggestion that it comes from parcere 'to spare' is a hypothesis rather than a proved link.
items.cn: 一种说法把 scarcitas 追溯到 parcus「节省的、俭省的」。parcus 的更深来源不确定；认为它出自 parcere「节省」的说法是假说，而非已证实的联系。

items.en: Scarcitas meant 'scarcity, scantiness'. On this account the noun passed into Old French as scarcete and then into English.
items.cn: scarcitas 意为「短缺、稀少」。按这一说法，该名词进入古法语作 scarcete，再进入英语。

items.en: Old French scarcete meant 'smallness, scantiness, stinginess' and English scarcity first carried that sense of meagre supply before widening to any shortage.
items.cn: 古法语 scarcete 意为「少、不足、吝啬」，英语 scarcity 最初带这种「供给寒酸」的意思，后扩为任何短缺。

items.en: The competing account connects the adjective scarce to Vulgar Latin excarpsus 'plucked out', from ex- 'out' plus carpere 'to pluck'. This account explains the adjective but does not settle the noun.
items.cn: 对立说法把形容词 scarce 连到俗拉丁 excarpsus「被摘出的」，出自 ex-「向外」加 carpere「摘取」。这一说法解释了形容词，却未能定下名词的来源。

items.en: From the nineteenth century classical economics made scarcity the central condition of economic life, and the word acquired its technical sense of finite means against unlimited wants.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，古典经济学把稀缺定为经济生活的核心条件，这个词于是获得「有限手段面对无限欲望」的技术义。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): the derivation is disputed between parcus and excarpsus, and no single earliest citation is fixed for the modern economic sense, so its first date is approximate; any older Indo-European forms offered for this family are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：词源在 parcus 与 excarpsus 之间存疑，现代经济义也没有公认的最早书证，首见年代只能约计；凡为这个词族给出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words that look close to scarcity but differ in part of speech, meaning or root; group two holds other nouns of not having enough, each with a different reason for the shortfall.
note.cn: 第一组是与 scarcity 形近、但词性、含义或词根不同的词；第二组是其他表示「不够」的名词，每一个的短缺原因都不同。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'hard to obtain in quantity'; scarcity is the noun built on it in meaning, even where the derivation is debated.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「数量稀少、难以取得」；scarcity 在语义上是它的名词形式，尽管词源仍有争议。

entries.definition: Means 'barely, hardly', not 'sparsely'; the adverb has drifted away from the idea of quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「几乎不、勉强」，而非「稀少地」；这个副词已偏离数量概念。

entries.definition: Thinly spread, from Latin sparsus 'scattered'; it looks close to scarce but shares no root with it.
entries.definitionCN: 分布稀疏的，出自拉丁 sparsus「散开的」；与 scarce 外形相近，但并无共同词根。

entries.definition: A rarer synonym of scarcity formed with -ness; it names the state without the economic overtones.
entries.definitionCN: 由 -ness 构成的较罕用同义词；它只指状态，不带经济学色彩。

entries.definition: A plain word for a supply that is below the amount required, usually temporary or local.
entries.definitionCN: 指供给低于所需数量的普通词，通常是临时或局部的。

entries.definition: An old word for a scarce supply, especially of food; it comes from dear in the sense of costly, not from scarcity.
entries.definitionCN: 指供给稀少、尤指食物的旧词；它出自表示「昂贵」的 dear，而非出自 scarcity。

entries.definition: A formal noun for a small number or amount, from Latin paucus 'few'; it stresses fewness rather than unmet demand.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，指数量很少，出自拉丁 paucus「少」；它强调数量少，而非需求未被满足。

entries.definition: The quality of being uncommon; a rare thing may be plentiful in absolute terms and still be uncommon in kind.
entries.definitionCN: 不常见的性质；稀见之物在绝对数量上可能很多，只是在种类上少见。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Scarcity is the noun of scarce; the -ity ending turns the adjective into a state.
normal.cn: scarcity 是 scarce 的名词，-ity 后缀把形容词变成状态。

normal.en: The economic sense is fixed in one phrase: limited resources against unlimited wants.
normal.cn: 经济义固定在一句话里：有限资源面对无限欲望。

normal.en: The family runs scarce, scarcely, scarceness, scarcity and water-scarce.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 scarce、scarcely、scarceness、scarcity 与 water-scarce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: water scarcity, food scarcity, resource scarcity, artificial scarcity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：水资源短缺、粮食短缺、资源稀缺、人为稀缺。

normal.en: Sparse looks like scarce but comes from sparsus 'scattered', so the two are false relatives.
normal.cn: sparse 看起来像 scarce，却出自 sparsus「散开的」，两者是假同源。

abstract.en: Picture the last basket on a table and every hand reaching at once.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上最后一筐，所有手同时伸过去。

abstract.en: Picture a day with more tasks than hours, so each choice costs another choice.
abstract.cn: 想象一天里任务多过小时，每个选择都要用另一个选择来换。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf kept almost empty on purpose so that the few items look precious.
abstract.cn: 想象货架故意留得几乎空着，好让剩下的几件显得珍贵。

examples.en: Classical economics treats scarcity as the reason choice is necessary.
examples.cn: 古典经济学把稀缺视为选择之所以必要的原因。

examples.en: The scarcity of rare earths reshaped the electronics supply chain.
examples.cn: 稀土资源的稀缺重塑了电子产业供应链。

examples.en: Artificial scarcity can keep a price high long after demand has fallen.
examples.cn: 人为稀缺可以在需求下降很久之后仍把价格维持在高位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「scarce（稀少）+ ity」——东西少、要的人多 → 稀缺、短缺

root: 古法语 scarcete < 拉丁 scarcitas「短缺」；词根一说为 parcus「俭省的」，另一说与俗拉丁 excarpsus「摘出的」（ex- + carpere）相关，两说并存未定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one relation: a supply is smaller than the demand on it. The word then becomes the foundation of economics, the state of a rare object, an ecological limit, a mindset, a shortage of time, of attention, a shortage made on purpose and finally a premium on price.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个关系展开：供给小于对它的需求。这个词随后成为经济学的基础、稀见物的状态、生态的限制、一种心态、时间与注意力的不足、有意制造的不足，最后是价格上的溢价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one last basket on an emptying table while more hands reach for it.
core.cn: 核心意象：空下去的桌上只剩最后一筐，伸过来的手却更多。

branches.en: THE GAP: the everyday shortfall and the founding condition of economics are the same relation formalised.
branches.cn: 缺口：日常的不足与经济学的出发点，是同一关系被形式化。

branches.en: FEWNESS: a rare object and a depleted habitat are both cases of supply falling.
branches.cn: 稀少：稀见之物与枯竭的栖息地，都是供给下降的情形。

branches.en: MIND: perception can produce the behaviour of scarcity before the shortage arrives.
branches.cn: 心态：感知可以在短缺到来之前就制造出稀缺的行为。

branches.en: NON-MATERIAL: hours and attention are fixed or finite supplies of their own.
branches.cn: 非实物：小时与注意力本身就是固定或有限的供给。

branches.en: MADE AND PRICED: scarcity can be staged, and rarity can be charged for.
branches.cn: 制造与定价：稀缺可以被安排出来，稀少也可以被收费。

intro.en: Scarcity is a noun formed with a Latin state suffix on a stem whose own origin is disputed, so the suffix is certain while the root is not.
intro.cn: scarcity 是用拉丁状态后缀构成的名称，词干本身的来源有争议，因此后缀确定而词根不确定。

latinIntro.en: The state suffix -itas gives English -ity in scarcity, rarity and paucity; the root is variously traced to parcus 'sparing' or to excarpsus 'plucked out'.
latinIntro.cn: 状态后缀 -itas 在 scarcity、rarity 与 paucity 中作英语 -ity；词根则有 parcus「俭省的」与 excarpsus「摘出的」两种追溯。

items.structure: Old French scars / escars (adjective, disputed origin)
items.example: Clean water was scarce after the drought.
items.exampleCN: 旱情之后洁净水很稀缺。

items.example: The suffix turns scarce into a named state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 scarce 变成一个有名称的状态。

items.example: Scarceness is the plainer twin of scarcity.
items.exampleCN: scarceness 是 scarcity 更朴素的双胞胎。

items.meaning: shortage; the state of being scarce
items.example: Scarcity raised the price of grain.
items.exampleCN: 稀缺抬高了谷物价格。

items.example: Good soil is scarce on the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 山脊上良田稀少。

items.example: She scarcely had time to eat.
items.exampleCN: 她几乎没时间吃饭。

items.example: The scarceness of fuel closed the mill.
items.exampleCN: 燃料的稀少让磨坊关了门。

items.meaning: charges raised because supply is short
items.meaningCN: 因供给短缺而提高的收费
items.example: Scarcity pricing cut peak demand.
items.exampleCN: 稀缺定价压低了高峰需求。

items.meaning: a shortage kept in place on purpose
items.example: The reissue was artificial scarcity.
items.exampleCN: 这次再版属于人为稀缺。

latinEntries.structure: parcus, parca, parcum (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 污染物；沾染物；使某物变得不纯或不宜使用的物质
definition_en: a substance that makes something impure, unsafe or unfit for its intended use by being present in it
core_image: 取样瓶里浮着一层薄薄的油膜，原本清澈的水面被这一点外来物搅得不再可信
scene: 检测员在水厂的取样瓶里发现一层薄薄的油膜，仪器读数随即报警。A single contaminant in the sample pushed the reading past the safety limit.
sceneCN: 这里 contaminant 指「混入某物、使其不纯或不宜使用的物质」（第 1 个义项：外来的沾染物使整体失去纯净）；句意为样本中一种污染物就把读数推过了安全限值。图中可辨识物件：取样瓶、油膜、检测仪、报警灯。

pos.zh: 污染物；沾染物（可数，指一种具体的污染物质）

senses.title: A substance that makes something impure
senses.titleCN: 使某物变得不纯的外来物质
senses.definition: any substance whose presence spoils the purity or quality of a material, medium or product
senses.definitionCN: 任何因其存在而破坏材料、介质或产品纯度与品质的物质
senses.example: A single contaminant in the sample pushed the reading past the safety limit.
senses.exampleCN: 样本中一种污染物就把读数推过了安全限值。
senses.why: The Latin root means 'to touch together', so a contaminant is literally something that has touched a clean body and left itself behind in it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「接触在一起」，因此 contaminant 字面上就是「碰过洁净之物并在其中留下自己的东西」。

senses.title: A pollutant in air, water or soil
senses.titleCN: 空气、水体或土壤中的污染物质
senses.definition: a substance present in an environmental medium at a level that harms organisms or uses
senses.definitionCN: 存在于环境介质中、其含量足以危害生物或用途的物质
senses.example: The aquifer held a solvent contaminant from the old factory.
senses.exampleCN: 含水层里存着老工厂留下的一种溶剂污染物。
senses.why: Environmental science adopted the word because it names the thing rather than the harm, which is measured separately.
senses.whyCN: 环境科学采用这个词，因为它命名的是物质本身，而危害另有指标衡量。

senses.title: A biological contaminant such as a microbe
senses.titleCN: 微生物等生物性沾染物
senses.definition: a bacterium, virus, fungus or other organism that makes a product or surface unsafe
senses.definitionCN: 使产品或表面变得不安全的细菌、病毒、真菌或其他生物
senses.example: A bacterial contaminant closed the production line for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一种细菌污染物让生产线停了一周。
senses.why: Living things contaminate as effectively as chemicals, and laboratories needed one word that covers both.
senses.whyCN: 活物与化学品一样能造成沾染，实验室需要一个词同时涵盖两者。

senses.title: A trace residue of chemicals
senses.titleCN: 残留的痕量化学物质
senses.definition: a pesticide, drug, heavy metal or solvent left at very low concentration in food, water or tissue
senses.definitionCN: 以极低浓度残留在食品、水或组织中的农药、药物、重金属或溶剂
senses.example: Regulators set a limit for each pesticide contaminant.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构为每种农药残留设定了限值。
senses.why: Modern instruments can find a few parts per billion, so the word now covers amounts far too small to see.
senses.whyCN: 现代仪器能检出十亿分之几，这个词于是涵盖了肉眼完全看不见的量。

senses.title: Foreign matter in food or medicine
senses.titleCN: 食品与药品中的外来异物
senses.definition: glass, metal, plastic or other matter that enters a product during handling and makes it unsafe
senses.definitionCN: 在加工过程中进入产品、使其不安全的玻璃、金属、塑料或其他物质
senses.example: A metal contaminant triggered the recall of the batch.
senses.exampleCN: 一种金属污染物触发了这批产品的召回。
senses.why: For manufacturers the word covers anything that should not be in the package, living or not.
senses.whyCN: 对制造商而言，这个词涵盖一切不该出现在包装里的东西，无论是否有生命。

senses.title: A radioactive contaminant
senses.titleCN: 放射性沾染物
senses.definition: a radionuclide deposited on a surface, in soil or in a body where it does not belong
senses.definitionCN: 沉积在不该出现的表面、土壤或人体内的放射性核素
senses.example: Workers mapped the radioactive contaminant around the old reactor.
senses.exampleCN: 工作人员标出了旧反应堆周围的放射性污染物。
senses.why: Radiation is invisible and persistent, so the word stresses location and unwanted presence rather than visible dirt.
senses.whyCN: 辐射看不见又持久，这个词于是强调位置与「不该在此」，而非看得见的脏污。

senses.title: A particle in a cleanroom or vacuum
senses.titleCN: 洁净室或真空中的微粒沾染物
senses.definition: a dust particle, fibre or molecular film that ruins a wafer, lens or vacuum process
senses.definitionCN: 使晶圆、镜片或真空工艺失效的尘粒、纤维或分子膜
senses.example: A sub-micron contaminant ruined the coating on the lens.
senses.exampleCN: 一粒亚微米级污染物毁掉了镜片镀膜。
senses.why: In manufacturing the threshold is not health but function: a particle too small to see can still break a circuit.
senses.whyCN: 在制造中，门槛不是健康而是功能：小到看不见的颗粒仍能毁掉电路。

senses.title: Abstract: anything that corrupts a clean system
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何使洁净系统失真的东西
senses.definition: a transferred use for an element that corrupts the purity of data, language or a process
senses.definitionCN: 转指使数据、语言或流程丧失纯净性的因素
senses.example: A stale record is a contaminant in the training set.
senses.exampleCN: 过时记录是训练集里的一种污染。
senses.why: The metaphor works because the physical image is general: a small foreign thing enters a clean body and changes what the body can be used for.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，是因为物理意象很通用：一小点外来物进入洁净的整体，改变了这个整体还能做什么。

intro.en: Contaminant is the noun use of the present participle of contaminate, which came to English from Latin by way of French. The root image is touching. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: contaminant 是 contaminate 现在分词的名词化用法，而 contaminate 经法语来自拉丁语。其词根意象是「接触」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Tangere meant 'to touch'. Its deeper origin is not established; the Indo-European root often proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: tangere 意为「触摸」。其更深来源未得到证明；常为它提出的印欧词根是重构，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus the touch root produced contamen 'contact, pollution', the idea of one thing being defiled by touching another.
items.cn: com-「共同」加「触摸」词根构成 contamen「接触、污染」，即一物因碰到另一物而被弄脏。

items.en: Contaminare meant 'to defile by contact, to corrupt'. It carried both the physical and the moral sense of making something unclean.
items.cn: contaminare 意为「因接触而弄脏、败坏」。它同时带有「使不洁」的物理义与道德义。

items.en: English contaminate appears in the sixteenth century, first of moral or ritual defilement and later of physical mixture.
items.cn: 英语 contaminate 出现于十六世纪，先指道德或仪式上的玷污，后指物理上的混入。

items.en: Contaminant became a separate noun in modern technical English, once laboratories needed a word for the offending substance itself rather than the act.
items.cn: 当实验室需要一个词来指「肇事的物质本身」而非动作时，contaminant 在现代技术英语中成为独立名词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date of the noun, deeper origin of tangere): the noun's first technical citation is not fixed, so its date is approximate; the pre-Latin origin of tangere is unsettled and any form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（该名词的首见年代、tangere 的更深词源）：这个名词最早的 technical 书证没有定论，年代只能约计；tangere 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，凡为其提出的形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same touch-root family that are easily mistaken for the noun; group two holds other words for unwanted material, each with a different reason for being unwanted.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「触摸」词根、容易被误当作本名词的各种形式；第二组是其他表示「不该有的物质」的词，各自「不该有」的理由不同。

entries.definition: The act or result of contaminating; it names the event or condition, while contaminant names the substance.
entries.definitionCN: 污染的动作或结果；它指事件或状态，而 contaminant 指物质。

entries.definition: To make impure by contact; it is the action that puts a contaminant into something.
entries.definitionCN: 因接触而使不纯；它是把污染物放进某物的动作。

entries.definition: Touching or communication, from the same tangere root but with no sense of defilement.
entries.definitionCN: 接触或联系，同出 tangere 词根，但不含「玷污」之义。

entries.definition: Spread of disease by contact, from contingere 'to touch upon'; it shares the touch root but follows a medical path.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病经接触传播，出自 contingere「触及」；它与 contaminant 同享触摸词根，却走的是医学路线。

entries.definition: A substance that harms the environment; a contaminant may be harmless in small amounts and still unfit a product.
entries.definitionCN: 危害环境的物质；污染物质量小时可能无害，却仍能使产品不合格。

entries.definition: Any foreign matter in a material, often harmless; it is a purity term rather than a safety term.
entries.definitionCN: 材料中混入的任何外来物，常为无害；它是纯度术语，而非安全术语。

entries.definition: A substance that is poisonous to living things; toxicity is its defining property, which a contaminant need not have.
entries.definitionCN: 对生物有毒的物质；毒性是它的定义属性，而污染物不一定有毒。

entries.definition: Something added to a product to cheapen or fake it; the motive is deception, not accidental mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 为降低成本或造假而加入产品的东西；其动机是欺骗，而非意外混入。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is tangere 'to touch': something touched the clean body and stayed in it.
normal.cn: 词根是 tangere「触摸」：某物碰过洁净之物并留在了里面。

normal.en: Contaminant is the thing, contamination is the process, contaminate is the act.
normal.cn: contaminant 是物，contamination 是过程，contaminate 是动作。

normal.en: The family runs contaminate, contamination, contaminated, decontaminate and contaminative.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 contaminate、contamination、contaminated、decontaminate 与 contaminative。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: chemical contaminant, biological contaminant, trace contaminant.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：化学污染物、生物污染物、痕量污染物。

normal.en: Contact and contagion share the touch root but carry no idea of impurity in the same way.
normal.cn: contact 与 contagion 共享触摸词根，但并不以同样的方式带有「不纯」之意。

abstract.en: Picture one drop of ink falling into a glass of clear water.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴墨落进一杯清水。

abstract.en: Picture a single wrong figure entering an otherwise clean ledger.
abstract.cn: 想象一个错数进入一本本来干净的账。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour passing through a room and changing what everyone repeats.
abstract.cn: 想象一则传言穿过一间屋子，改变了每个人复述的内容。

examples.en: The filter removes the contaminant before the water reaches the tap.
examples.cn: 过滤器在水到达龙头之前去除污染物。

examples.en: Each contaminant has its own detection limit and removal method.
examples.cn: 每种污染物都有自己的检出限与去除方法。

examples.en: A biological contaminant can multiply after it enters the product.
examples.cn: 生物污染物进入产品之后还可能增殖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「con（共同）+ tamin（接触）+ ant」——碰到干净东西、把它弄脏的那一位 → 污染物

root: 拉丁 contaminare「弄脏、败坏」< contamen「接触、污染」= com-（共同）+ tangere「触摸」；tangere 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one intrusion: a foreign thing touches a clean body, purity is lost, fitness is lost, the intruder is measured, and finally the same shape is used for corrupted data.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次侵入展开：外来物碰触洁净体，纯净性失去，可用性失去，侵入者被计量，最后同一形态被用于被污染的数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one drop of oil floating in a bottle of clear water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一瓶清水里浮着一滴油。

branches.en: PURITY AND ENVIRONMENT: the general definition and the environmental case both name the intruder, not the harm.
branches.cn: 纯净与环境：总定义与环境情形命名的都是侵入者，而非危害。

branches.en: LIVING AND TRACE: a microbe and a residue are both small enough to escape the eye.
branches.cn: 活物与痕量：微生物与残留都小到肉眼难辨。

branches.en: PRODUCT SAFETY: what should never be in the package defines this sense.
branches.cn: 产品安全：本不该出现在包装里的东西，界定了这个义项。

branches.en: LOCATION AND FUNCTION: radiation in the wrong place and a particle in a cleanroom both ruin by being where they are.
branches.cn: 位置与功能：错处的辐射与洁净室里的颗粒，都因「待在那里」而毁事。

branches.en: TRANSFER: a bad record contaminates a dataset as oil contaminates water.
branches.cn: 转移：坏记录污染数据集，正如油污染水。

intro.en: Contaminant is a Latin-derived noun with a prefix, a touch root and a participial suffix, so it can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: contaminant 是拉丁来源名词，含前缀、触摸词根与分词后缀，可以逐语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin tangere 'to touch' gives contact, contagion, contiguous and tangible; con- adds 'together' and -ant marks the thing that does the action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tangere「触摸」衍生 contact、contagion、contiguous 与 tangible；con- 添「共同」，-ant 标出执行动作之物。

items.example: The prefix marks contact between two things.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出两物之间的接触。

items.example: The root carries the idea of contact.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「接触」的意思。

items.example: Contamen named the defilement left by touch.
items.exampleCN: contamen 指接触留下的污损。

items.example: The verb entered English as contaminate.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词以 contaminate 进入英语。

items.meaning: the thing or person that does
items.example: The suffix makes the verb into the offending thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成「肇事的物」。

items.example: One contaminant spoiled the whole tank.
items.exampleCN: 一种污染物毁掉了整罐。

items.meaning: the act or state of being defiled
items.example: Contamination closed the well.
items.exampleCN: 污染使这口井关闭。

items.example: Teams decontaminated the site.
items.exampleCN: 队伍对场地进行了去污。

items.example: The two surfaces were in contact.
items.exampleCN: 两个表面相互接触。

items.example: Contagion spread through the barracks.
items.exampleCN: 传染病在营房里蔓延。

definition_zh: 污染物；进入环境并造成危害的物质
definition_en: a substance introduced into air, water or soil that damages living things or the uses of that environment
core_image: 清晨的烟囱吐出一股灰白烟柱，顺着风慢慢压低到居民区屋顶的高度
scene: 工厂的排烟口在清晨吐出灰白色烟柱，顺着风散向居民区。The smokestack released a pollutant that settled over the nearby houses.
sceneCN: 这里 pollutant 指「进入空气并造成危害的物质」（第 2 个义项：排入大气后危害健康或环境的物质）；句意为烟囱排放的一种污染物沉降到附近房屋上空。图中可辨识物件：烟囱、烟柱、风向、居民区屋顶。

pos.zh: 污染物；污染物质（可数，指一种具体污染物）

senses.title: A substance that damages the environment
senses.titleCN: 对环境造成危害的物质
senses.definition: any substance whose entry into the environment harms organisms, materials or human health
senses.definitionCN: 进入环境后危害生物、材料或人类健康的任何物质
senses.example: The smokestack released a pollutant that settled over the nearby houses.
senses.exampleCN: 烟囱排放的一种污染物沉降到附近房屋上空。
senses.why: Pollutant is pollute plus -ant, so it names the agent that does the polluting rather than the damaged state.
senses.whyCN: pollutant 是 pollute 加 -ant，因此它命名的是「执行污染的那个东西」，而非被污染的状态。

senses.title: An air pollutant
senses.titleCN: 空气污染物
senses.definition: a gas or particle in the air at a level that harms health, visibility or crops
senses.definitionCN: 在空气中达到危害健康、能见度或作物的浓度的气体或颗粒
senses.example: Ground-level ozone is the pollutant that closes the parks in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 近地面臭氧是夏天让公园关闭的那种污染物。
senses.why: Air was the first medium regulated in law, so the word's most familiar sense is the smoke and gas that enters it.
senses.whyCN: 空气是最早被立法管制的介质，因此这个词最熟悉的义项就是进入空气的烟与气体。

senses.title: A water pollutant
senses.titleCN: 水体污染物
senses.definition: a substance in rivers, lakes or groundwater that harms aquatic life or drinking supply
senses.definitionCN: 河流、湖泊或地下水中危害水生生物或饮用水供给的物质
senses.example: Fertiliser runoff is a water pollutant that feeds algal blooms.
senses.exampleCN: 化肥径流是一种水体污染物，会滋养藻华。
senses.why: Water carries substances far from their source, so the word shifted from the pipe to the whole catchment.
senses.whyCN: 水把物质从源头带到很远，这个词于是从管子转向整个流域。

senses.title: A soil pollutant
senses.titleCN: 土壤污染物
senses.definition: a substance that accumulates in soil and harms plants, soil life or the food chain
senses.definitionCN: 在土壤中累积、危害植物、土壤生物或食物链的物质
senses.example: Lead was a soil pollutant around every old road.
senses.exampleCN: 铅曾是每条老路周边的一种土壤污染物。
senses.why: Soil holds what water washes out of the air, so the pollutant persists long after the source has gone.
senses.whyCN: 土留住了水从空气中洗下的东西，因此污染源消失很久之后污染仍在。

senses.title: A pollutant that is not a substance
senses.titleCN: 非物质的污染物：噪声、光、热
senses.definition: an excess of noise, light, heat or radiation that degrades the environment without adding matter
senses.definitionCN: 过量的噪声、光、热或辐射，虽不添加物质，却使环境退化
senses.example: Light at night is a pollutant for migrating birds.
senses.exampleCN: 夜间的灯光对迁徙鸟类是一种污染。
senses.why: The word's frame is 'something added that harms', and energy can be added as well as matter.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的框架是「加了某物而造成危害」，而被加进去的除了物质也可以是能量。

senses.title: A biological pollutant
senses.titleCN: 生物性污染物
senses.definition: a pathogen or introduced organism that harms native life or human health
senses.definitionCN: 危害本地生物或人类健康的病原体或外来生物
senses.example: Ballast water carried a biological pollutant across the ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 压载水把一种生物污染物带过了大洋。
